# ADR-NNNN: <short imperative title>

## Status
Proposed | Accepted | Superseded by ADR-NNNN | Deprecated

## Date
YYYY-MM-DD

## Context

What forces are at play? Requirements, constraints, the shape of the problem. Write this
so someone with no memory of the discussion can judge whether the decision still holds.

State the constraint that actually drives the decision, not a list of everything true
about the system. If one fact makes the answer obvious, lead with it.

## Decision

What we are doing. Present tense, active voice, specific enough to act on.

## Alternatives Considered

For each real alternative — not straw men:

### <Alternative>
- Pros: …
- Cons: …
- Rejected: the single reason it lost.

An ADR with no credible alternatives is a note, not a decision record.

## Consequences

What becomes true as a result. Include the bad parts — the cost accepted, the new
constraint, the thing that gets harder. An ADR that only lists benefits is not being
honest and will not be trusted later.

## Revisit when

Concrete triggers that would make this decision wrong. Thresholds, scale points, or events
— not "if requirements change".
